notes: Normalization adjusts reported net income to Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE) and adjusted EBITDA by adding back owner compensation, depreciation, interest, taxes, one-time expenses, and discretionary/personal expenses.
SDE = Net Income + Owner's Full Compensation + D&A + Interest + Taxes + One-Time Items + Discretionary Items.
Adjusted EBITDA = Net Income + (Owner Comp − Market Salary) + D&A + Interest + Taxes + One-Time Items + Discretionary Items = SDE − Market Salary.
2024 Adjusted EBITDA: $1,717,000 (SDE) − $165,000 (market GM salary) = $1,552,000.
Check: the note above states 2024 SDE as $1,552,000; the add-backs listed here compute $1,717,000.
SDE has grown 63% from 2021 to 2024 ($1,055,000 to $1,717,000). Adjusted EBITDA has grown 74% ($890,000 to $1,552,000).

SDE margin: 13.7% (2021), 14.7% (2022), 16.0% (2023), 17.5% (2024). Adjusted EBITDA margin: 11.6% (2021), 12.8% (2022), 14.2% (2023), 15.8% (2024). Strong margin expansion driven by revenue growth, equipment efficiency, and pricing discipline.

Owner compensation: Gord McAllister's $180,000 T4 salary is the only owner compensation on the P&L. Dividends ($40,000 in 2021-2022, $60,000 in 2023-2024) are distributions of after-tax profit and are not add-backs.

Replacement GM salary: A general manager for a $10M custom fabrication business in the Edmonton/Nisku market would cost approximately $165,000 (base $140,000 + benefits/bonus ~18%). This is a conservative estimate; some buyers may use a lower figure ($120-140K for an operations manager if the buyer's corporate team handles sales and finance).

One-time items: The 2024 crane rebuild ($64,000) and shareholder agreement legal fees ($18,000) are genuine one-time expenses. The 2022 Silverthorn bad debt ($22,000) is also non-recurring (single receivership event).

Discretionary items: Owner's truck/personal expenses ($28,000), hockey sponsorship ($12,000), and Donna's salary above market ($17,000) are discretionary and would not recur under new ownership. Total discretionary add-backs: $57,000 in 2024.

Donna's salary: She is paid $62,000/year for part-time bookkeeping (per accountant's notes). A market-rate part-time bookkeeper would cost ~$45,000. The $17,000 excess is added back. A buyer may eliminate the role entirely and use their own accounting staff or outsource to the accountant.

No add-backs for 2021-2023 discretionary items: The seller's add-back list only covers 2024. Truck, hockey, and Donna's excess salary likely existed in prior years but are not quantified. The 2021-2023 SDE and adjusted EBITDA figures are conservative (understated) as a result.

Related-party rent: The $336,000/year rent (2024) paid to McAllister Properties Ltd. is at market per an independent market rent opinion (December 2021). No add-back is appropriate. A buyer can either purchase the building at $4.1M (appraised value, November 2024) or sign a new 10-year lease at $12.50/sq ft net ($350,000/year) with two 5-year renewal options.

Capital expenditures: Maintenance capex is estimated at $200-250,000/year. 2024 capex of $430,000 includes the new plasma table ($468,000, growth capex). Buyers should budget for replacement of the 110-ton brake (~$180,000) and old plasma table within 2 years.

Working capital: Net working capital (cash-free, debt-free) is $1,237,000 at Dec 31 2024 (12.6% of revenue). This is appropriate for the business and should be maintained at closing (peg at average of year-end NWC).

Debt: Long-term debt of $1,342,000 (Dec 31 2024) is modest (0.8x adjusted EBITDA). The equipment term loan matures November 2027; vehicle/equipment loans mature 2026-2028. A buyer can assume or refinance the debt.

Backlog: Signed backlog is $3.1M at May 31, 2025 (per WIP report). Open quotes total $2.2M (historical win rate ~35%). YTD revenue (Jan-May 2025) is ~$4.18M, up 8% vs prior year. The business has strong momentum.

Key risks: (1) Larkspur (18% of revenue) is consolidating vendors in 2026 (8 to 3 approved fabricators); Ridgeline expects to make the short list but re-bid is required. (2) Westlock job ($1.1M) is verbally awarded but PO not yet issued (board approval pending). (3) Devin (chief estimator) has no employment contract or non-compete; retention bonus recommended. (4) Two senior welders retiring in 2-3 years. (5) Equipment replacement needs (110-ton brake, old plasma table, forklift).

Seller's asking price: $6.5M for the business (excluding real estate). At 2024 adjusted EBITDA of $1,552,000, this is 4.2x. At 2024 SDE of $1,717,000, this is 3.8x. Both multiples are reasonable for a profitable, growing, CWB-certified fabrication business with diversified revenue and strong backlog.

Reported net income does not tie to the Income Statement rows — 2024: Income Statement 936,410 vs reported 896,410 (+40,000). The normalization starts from the reported figure; review the Income Statement reclassification before relying on either.

addbacks.label: Owner compensation (President — Gord McAllister)
addbacks.description: Owner's pay $180,000 (2024) less a $165,000 market salary for the role: the difference counts for EBITDA and SDE; the market salary is added back for SDE only. Gord McAllister's T4 salary of $180,000/year as President. A replacement general manager for a $10M fabrication business in Alberta would cost approximately $165,000 (base salary $140,000 + benefits/bonus ~18%). The $15,000 excess is added back to adjusted EBITDA; the full $180,000 is added back to SDE.

addbacks.label: Owner compensation (President — Gord McAllister) — market salary
addbacks.description: SDE adds back the owner's full pay; this is the market-salary part. A buyer who hires someone for the role pays it, so it is not added back to EBITDA.

addbacks.label: Depreciation & amortization
addbacks.description: Book amortization of tangible assets. Non-cash expense added back to EBITDA and SDE.

addbacks.label: Interest expense
addbacks.description: Interest on long-term debt (equipment term loan and vehicle/equipment loans). Added back to EBITDA and SDE.

addbacks.label: Income taxes
addbacks.description: Current income taxes (taxes payable method). Added back to EBITDA and SDE.

addbacks.label: Crane rebuild (one-time)
addbacks.description: Rebuild of both 10-ton overhead cranes in 2024 (new hoists, end trucks, pendants). Deducted as current expense; will not recur for ~20 years. One-time add-back.

addbacks.label: Legal fees — shareholder agreement (one-time)
addbacks.description: Legal fees for November 2024 amendment to unanimous shareholder agreement (waived Luis's ROFR for sale). One-time expense.

addbacks.label: Owner's truck & personal expenses
addbacks.description: Owner's 3/4-ton pickup truck expenses (fuel, insurance, personal use, season tickets) run through the company. Excluded from normalized EBITDA and SDE.

addbacks.label: Hockey sponsorship (discretionary)
addbacks.description: Sponsorship of Leduc junior hockey team. Discretionary marketing expense; excluded from normalized EBITDA and SDE.

addbacks.label: Donna's salary above market (bookkeeper)
addbacks.description: Donna McAllister (owner's spouse) performs part-time bookkeeping and is paid $62,000/year. Market rate for a part-time bookkeeper is estimated at $45,000. The $17,000 excess is discretionary and added back.

addbacks.label: Silverthorn bad debt (non-recurring)
addbacks.description: 2022 bad debt of $22,000 from Silverthorn Energy Services receivership (September 2022). Single event; 2023 and 2024 bad debts ($9,000 and $12,000) are ordinary small write-offs. Non-recurring add-back for 2022 only.
